task: Round 9 bypass hunt. Construct a WORKING bypass of the admission-binding mechanism at HEAD (4ec13b5) and demonstrate it executably, or prove by exhaustion of the attack surface that you cannot. Rounds 1 through 6 produced working attacks; rounds 7 and 8 did not. Your target is the whole path: admit_agent.py minting, the per-(run, agent_id) flock in subagent_stop_validate.py, the three-state receipt rule in subagent_start_context.py, the forward attribution sweep and pending-carve-out refusal in validate_harness.py, merge_results.py, and scrub_admission_proof.py. Attack ideas to exhaust rather than a checklist to tick: confusion between two open receipts in one run and across runs; reuse of a consumed receipt; a receipt reopened under --reopen; the --agent-id-unknown mode where no mint-time agent guard is constructible; symlink and TOCTOU races on the lock path and the receipt path; a malformed or truncated ADMISSIONS.jsonl line; an assignment whose result_path collides with another's; a result written before Stop and swapped after; and the retry path where a BLOCKED stop leaves a receipt open while a live token sits in a captured event. Note explicitly that harness and subagents share one OS user, so deliberate forgery of repo-local artifacts is a STATED residual and does not count as a novel finding on its own -- what counts is a bypass that survives the checks as written, or one that a plausible operator error triggers without intent. Build negative fixtures for anything you find. Do not modify production code, the Rust tree, or src/rabbit/decoupling/_independent_noqke.py.
